rules.sentence: Postnatally, Jacobsen syndrome should be suspected in infants with congenital heart disease and extracardiac anomalies, particularly if thrombocytopenia or easy bleeding is present.
Jacobsen syndrome should also be considered in patients with hypoplastic left heart syndrome, as the incidence of hypoplastic left heart syndrome is higher in Jacobsen syndrome.
Postnatal genetic testing can be performed using FISH or chromosomal microarray.[2]
